# Discoverability score: what it is and how it works

*ReachKit*

:::answer

It combines answerability, presence, and foundations into one figure. A low score means buyers asking ChatGPT or Google's AI about your market are being sent to rivals instead of you.

:::takeaways
- The discoverability score is one number summarising how findable a business is in AI answers and Google search.
- It is built from three parts: answerability, presence, and foundations.

## What is the discoverability score?

The discoverability score is a number out of 100 that stands in for a simple question: when a buyer asks AI or Google about your market, do you show up? It's not a vanity metric. It's built from how a site performs across the searches and AI questions that matter to its market.

A scan of one site put it plainly:

> 47 /100 Hard to find — and we'll show you the fixes that move it. — [ReachKit](https://reachkit.app/signin)

That's a low score, and the business explains why in the same breath: it comes with the fixes, not just the number. A score on its own is a diagnosis. The point is what moves it.

## How is the discoverability score calculated?

The score comes from reading a site, reading its access rules, finding its market and rivals, checking the biggest searches in that market, and asking AI a set of questions about it. Each of those checks feeds into three things: answerability, presence, and foundations.

Answerability asks whether a site's pages answer the questions buyers ask, in plain language an AI model can lift and use. Presence asks how often the business turns up at all, across both AI answers and Google results. Foundations asks whether anything technical is blocking access — pages AI readers can't reach, or a site structure that hides the content that does exist.

One dashboard view shows how this plays out over time, tracking a score alongside the raw inputs behind it:

That example shows a score of 62, up 8 points, alongside AI answers naming the business for 2 of the tracked questions and 17 pages published. The score moves because those underlying counts move — more searches appear in, more AI answers name the business, more pages are live.

## What affects the score, and what are its limits?

The score is not a single lever. It reflects several separate counts, and each one can be held down by a different problem — missing pages, pages that read like brochures instead of answering questions, or AI readers being blocked outright.

| Factor | What it measures | What holds it down |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answerability | Whether pages answer buyer questions directly | Pages that read like brochures instead of answering questions |
| Presence | How often the business appears across AI answers and Google | Missing pages that answer questions your market asks |
| Foundations | Whether AI and search can access the site at all | AI readers blocked, or access rules that shut them out |

The score is also tied to a fixed set of checks: the biggest searches in a market, and a fixed set of questions asked of AI directly. It isn't an open-ended crawl of the internet — it's a bounded measurement, re-run on a schedule, so it can be tracked week over week rather than treated as a one-time grade.

## What does a discoverability score look like in practice?

One published scan shows a score of 62, up 8 points from the prior measurement, with the business appearing in AI answers for 2 of the tracked questions and having published 17 pages. A separate scan shows a lower score, 47 out of 100, described plainly as hard to find.

Both examples share the same shape: a number, a direction of movement, and a count of how many of the tracked AI questions name the business. That's the whole point of the score — it isn't abstract, it ties back to specific questions buyers ask and specific pages that do or don't answer them.

## What else is the discoverability score connected to?

The score doesn't move by itself. It's tied directly to page publishing — each new page that answers a buyer question is a chance to appear in another AI answer or search result, and the weekly re-measurement is what shows whether that happened.

*Buyer questions, stored with the page (`drafts.meta.faq`):*

**Is the discoverability score the same as a Google ranking?**

No. It's a separate measurement that combines how a site appears across both AI answers and Google search, built from answerability, presence, and foundations checks. A ranking position is not part of it.

**How often is the discoverability score updated?**

The score is re-measured weekly, alongside a weekly movement email showing what changed. That's tied to the pace of page publishing, since new pages are what typically shift the underlying counts.

**Do I need an account to see my discoverability score?**

No. A free scan measures the score without an account, and the report is kept at a permanent public link.

**Can the discoverability score go down?**

Yes, since it reflects live measurement of searches and AI answers rather than a fixed grade. A market can shift, or rivals can publish new content, which is part of why it's re-measured weekly rather than once.

**What counts as a good discoverability score?**

The pack does not state a fixed threshold for what counts as good; published examples range from a low score described as hard to find up to a higher score with more AI answers naming the business, each judged against how many tracked searches and AI questions surface it.
